name: Nakasendo: Magome to Tsumago (中山道 馬籠・妻籠)
why: The best kept stretch of the Edo-period highway: from one wooden post town over a forest pass to another, with a free teahouse halfway.
book: Free. Bus from Nakatsugawa station to Magome; from Tsumago a bus goes to Nagiso station. Same-day luggage forwarding between the two tourist offices runs late March to late November.
water: Vending machines and shops in both towns; the Ichikokutochi teahouse serves tea. Carry 1 litre.
dangers: Cobbles and steps are slippery when wet, and icy in winter.
Bears live in the forest: bells hang along the trail, ring them.
Paved road crossings: watch for cars.
turnaround: None needed: if you are tired at Magome pass, the bus road is next to it.

points.name: Magome post town
points.note: From the bus stop the route climbs the steep stone street of Magome-juku, past the water wheel and the inns, then leaves the town at the lookout.

points.name: Magome pass (Magome-toge)
points.note: The top of the walk, about 800 m, now the border of Gifu and Nagano. From here it is downhill to Tsumago.

points.name: Ichikokutochi teahouse
points.note: An old farmhouse where volunteers serve free tea to walkers, beside the site of the Edo timber checkpoint.

points.name: Odaki and Medaki falls
points.note: The 'male and female' falls, a few steps off the path in the cedar forest.

points.name: Tsumago post town
points.note: A whole street of Edo-period wooden inns, closed to cars by day. Pick up forwarded luggage at the tourist office.
